questions.question:
The Deployment `payment-api` in the namespace `trbl-deploy` should run `2` replicas, but none of its Pods ever become Ready.

Investigate and fix **all** problems so that both replicas are Running and Ready.

- The container image must be `nginx:1.25-alpine`
- Keep the readiness probe (do not remove it), but make sure it checks the port nginx actually listens on

verification.description: Deployment uses image nginx:1.25-alpine
Readiness probe is kept and targets port 80
Both replicas are Ready

questions.question:
In the namespace `trbl-svc`, the Deployment `web` is running correctly, but the Service `web-svc` does not route any traffic to it. Requests from the Pod `client` (e.g. `wget -qO- -T 3 http://web-svc`) time out or fail.

Fix the **Service** so that `http://web-svc` (port `80`) returns the nginx page from the `client` Pod.

Do **not** modify the Deployment `web`.

verification.description: Service selects the web Pods (endpoints exist) and Deployment is unchanged
Service port 80 forwards to container port 80
client Pod can reach http://web-svc

questions.question:
The Pods of the Deployment `batch-processor` in the namespace `trbl-sched` are stuck in `Pending`.

Find out why with `kubectl describe` / events, then fix the Deployment so that both replicas run:

- Remove the node constraint that no node in the cluster satisfies
- Set the container CPU request to `100m` (keep the memory request `64Mi` unchanged)

verification.description: Impossible nodeSelector removed
CPU request is 100m and memory request still 64Mi
Both replicas are available

questions.question:
The Deployment `order-worker` in the namespace `trbl-config` cannot start its container (check the Pod status and events).

**Without modifying the Deployment**, fix the problem:

1. Create the missing Secret `order-db` with the key `password` and the value `Sup3rS3cret!`
2. The ConfigMap `order-config` already exists, but it does not contain the key the Deployment expects. Add that key with the value `orders` (keep the existing keys)

The Deployment must end up with `1` available replica.

verification.description: Secret order-db has password=Sup3rS3cret!
ConfigMap provides queue_name=orders and keeps existing keys
Deployment unchanged and 1 replica available

questions.question:
The Pod `audit-app` in the namespace `logging` has two containers: `app` and `shipper`.

1. Write **every** log line of the container `app` that contains the word `ERROR` to the file `/tmp/exam/q5/errors.log` on `ckad9999`. Lines from the `shipper` container must not be included.
2. Write the name of the node on which `audit-app` is running to `/tmp/exam/q5/node.txt` (just the node name).

verification.description: errors.log contains exactly the ERROR lines of container app
node.txt contains the node running audit-app

questions.question:
Three Pods with the label `app=analytics` are running in the namespace `metrics-lab`.

Using the Metrics API (`kubectl top`), find the Pod with label `app=analytics` that consumes the **most CPU** and write its name to `/tmp/exam/q6/top-pod.txt` on `ckad9999`.

Note: metrics can take a minute to appear after the Pods start.

verification.description: top-pod.txt names the highest-CPU analytics Pod

questions.question:
The worker node `k3d-cluster-agent-0` needs to go down for maintenance.

1. Mark `k3d-cluster-agent-0` as unschedulable
2. Safely evict all workloads from it (DaemonSet-managed Pods may stay)

After the maintenance preparation, the Deployment `maint-web` in the namespace `maintenance` must still have `3` Ready replicas, none of them on `k3d-cluster-agent-0`.

Do **not** delete the node. You should not need `--force`.

verification.description: k3d-cluster-agent-0 is unschedulable (and still exists)
maint-web has 3 Ready replicas, none on k3d-cluster-agent-0

questions.question:
Configure RBAC for two teams:

1. Create a ClusterRole `node-viewer` that allows `get`, `list` and `watch` on `nodes` and `persistentvolumes`. Bind it to the **user** `jane` with a ClusterRoleBinding named `jane-node-viewer`.
2. In the namespace `rbac-lab`, create a Role `deploy-manager` that allows `get`, `list`, `create`, `update`, `patch` and `delete` on `deployments`. Bind it to the **group** `developers` with a RoleBinding named `developers-deploy-manager`.

Verify with `kubectl auth can-i ... --as jane` and `--as someone --as-group developers`.

verification.description: jane can read nodes and PVs cluster-wide but not modify them
developers can manage deployments only in rbac-lab
RBAC objects use the required names and subject kinds

questions.question:
Extend the Kubernetes API with a CustomResourceDefinition:

- Name: `backups.ops.example.com`, group `ops.example.com`, kind `Backup`, plural `backups`, singular `backup`, short name `bk`
- Scope: `Namespaced`, single version `v1` (served and storage)
- Schema: `spec.schedule` of type `string` (required) and `spec.retentionDays` of type `integer` with a minimum of `1`

Then create a `Backup` named `nightly` in the namespace `crd-lab` with `schedule: "0 2 * * *"` and `retentionDays: 7`.

`kubectl get bk -n crd-lab` must list it.

verification.description: CRD has correct names, group and scope
CRD v1 schema validates schedule (string, required) and retentionDays (integer, min 1)
Backup nightly exists with the requested values

questions.question:
Two Deployments, `shop` (label `app=shop`) and `api` (label `app=api`), are running in the namespace `ingress-lab`. Both listen on port `80`.

1. Create a ClusterIP Service `shop-svc` exposing `shop` on port `80`
2. Create a ClusterIP Service `api-svc` exposing `api` on port `8080` (forwarding to container port `80`)
3. Create an Ingress `shop-ingress` with ingress class `traefik` for the host `shop.example.local`:
   - path `/api` (pathType `Prefix`) → `api-svc:8080`
   - path `/` (pathType `Prefix`) → `shop-svc:80`

verification.description: Services shop-svc and api-svc are correct and have endpoints
Ingress shop-ingress routes / and /api correctly

questions.question:
The namespace `np-db` contains a Pod `db` (label `app=db`) exposed by the Service `db` on port `80`.

1. Create a NetworkPolicy `default-deny-ingress` in `np-db` that denies **all** ingress traffic to every Pod in the namespace
2. Create a NetworkPolicy `allow-backend-api` in `np-db` that allows ingress to Pods with label `app=db` on TCP port `80` **only** from Pods with label `role=api` that run in namespaces labeled `team=backend`

Test Pods already exist: `np-backend/api` (should be allowed), `np-backend/worker` and `np-other/api` (should be denied).

verification.description: default-deny-ingress selects all Pods and denies ingress
allow-backend-api combines namespace and pod selector on TCP 80
Traffic is allowed only from np-backend/api

questions.question:
Create a DaemonSet `node-agent` in the namespace `ds-lab` that runs one Pod on **every** node of the cluster (including the control-plane node):

- Pod label: `app=node-agent`
- Container `agent`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'while true; do sleep 3600; done'`
- Mount the host directory `/var/log` **read-only** at `/host/log` (volume name `varlog`)
- Resource requests: CPU `10m`, memory `16Mi`

verification.description: DaemonSet spec is correct
A Ready node-agent Pod runs on every node

questions.question:
In the namespace `batch-lab`:

1. Create a CronJob `log-cleanup` that runs every `15` minutes with:
   - container `cleanup`, image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'echo cleaning logs; sleep 5'`
   - `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`
   - keep `2` successful and `1` failed Job in history
   - Jobs are retried at most `2` times (`backoffLimit`) and killed after `60` seconds (`activeDeadlineSeconds`)
   - Pod `restartPolicy: Never`
2. Without waiting for the schedule, trigger a Job named `log-cleanup-manual` **from the CronJob** and make sure it completes successfully.

verification.description: CronJob log-cleanup spec is correct
Job log-cleanup-manual was created from the CronJob
Job log-cleanup-manual completed successfully

questions.question:
Create a Pod `web-logger` in the namespace `sidecar-lab` that runs on the node `k3d-cluster-server-0`:

- Two `emptyDir` volumes: `html` and `logs`
- Init container `setup` (`busybox:1.36`) that writes the text `Hello CKA` to `/work/index.html` (volume `html` mounted at `/work`)
- **Native sidecar** container `log-tailer` (`busybox:1.36`), defined as an init container with `restartPolicy: Always`, running `tail -F /var/log/nginx/access.log` (volume `logs` mounted at `/var/log/nginx`)
- Main container `nginx` (`nginx:1.25`) mounting `html` at `/usr/share/nginx/html` and `logs` at `/var/log/nginx`

`curl localhost` inside the `nginx` container must return `Hello CKA`, and the request must appear in the logs of `log-tailer`.

verification.description: Pod runs on k3d-cluster-server-0 and is Ready
setup init container and log-tailer native sidecar configured
nginx serves Hello CKA and log-tailer sees the request

questions.question:
In the namespace `storage-ops`, the PersistentVolumeClaim `ledger-data` holds important data. Its dynamically provisioned PersistentVolume would be **deleted** together with the claim.

1. Change the reclaim policy of the PersistentVolume bound to `ledger-data` to `Retain`
2. Add the label `tier=critical` to that PersistentVolume
3. Write the name of that PersistentVolume to `/tmp/exam/q15/pv-name.txt` on `ckad9999`

Do not delete or recreate the PVC.

verification.description: PV bound to ledger-data has reclaim policy Retain
PV is labeled tier=critical
pv-name.txt contains the PV name

questions.question:
A CI system needs read-only access to the namespace `ci`.

1. Create a ServiceAccount `ci-bot` in the namespace `ci`
2. Create a long-lived token Secret `ci-bot-token` (type `kubernetes.io/service-account-token`) for `ci-bot`
3. Create a RoleBinding `ci-bot-view` in `ci` that grants the built-in ClusterRole `view` to `ci-bot`
4. Create the kubeconfig file `/tmp/exam/q16/ci-bot.kubeconfig` on `ckad9999` containing:
   - a cluster `ckx` using the same API server and CA as your current kubeconfig
   - a user `ci-bot` authenticating with the token from `ci-bot-token`
   - a context `ci-context` (cluster `ckx`, user `ci-bot`, namespace `ci`) set as the **current context**

`kubectl --kubeconfig /tmp/exam/q16/ci-bot.kubeconfig get pods` must work.

verification.description: ServiceAccount ci-bot and token Secret ci-bot-token exist
RoleBinding ci-bot-view grants ClusterRole view in ci
kubeconfig works with context ci-context and read-only access

questions.question:
The nodes `k3d-cluster-server-0` and `k3d-cluster-agent-1` are labeled with the zone key `topology.ckx.io/zone` (`zone-a` and `zone-b`).

Create a Deployment `spread-web` in the namespace `spread-lab`:

- `4` replicas, image `nginx:1.25`, Pod label `app=spread-web`
- A topology spread constraint with `maxSkew: 1` over the key `topology.ckx.io/zone`, `whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule`, selecting Pods with `app=spread-web`

All 4 replicas must be Running and evenly spread across the two zones.

verification.description: Topology spread constraint configured
4 replicas Running, 2 per zone

questions.question:
Pods of the Deployment `resolver` in the namespace `trbl-dns` cannot resolve any Service names, e.g. `nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local` fails.

Fix the Deployment so its Pods use the **cluster DNS** again (do not hard-code the CoreDNS IP).

verification.description: dnsPolicy uses cluster DNS without hard-coded nameservers
Pods can resolve kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local
